title: English 3 · Writing Baseline ✍️
subject: Writing
source_note: Baseline writing sample: one creative and one persuasive task, 20 minutes each like the 40-minute exam block. Marked by Claude with wiki/English/Writing_Rubric.md after export.

questions.stem:
Write a story that begins with this sentence:

“The door had been locked for as long as anyone could remember, until this morning.”
tips: Plan: who is the main character, what's the problem, how does it end?
Show feelings through actions ('her hands shook') instead of naming them ('she was scared').
One strong setting detail beats five weak ones.
Finish the story: a rushed or missing ending loses marks.
checklist: I used at least three precise, interesting words
I varied how my sentences start
I checked spelling and punctuation at the end
My story has a clear beginning, problem and ending
questions.technique: Plan, write, check: 3 min / 15 min / 2 min.
questions.source: ACER SEHS skill description: Writing, two tasks in 40 minutes

questions.stem:
Some people think students should be allowed to use their mobile phones at school during lunchtime. Others think phones should stay switched off all day.

Write a persuasive piece giving YOUR opinion. Try to convince the reader.
tips: Say your opinion clearly in the first paragraph.
Give 2–3 reasons, each in its own paragraph, with an example.
Answer one argument from the other side ('Some people say… however…').
End with a strong conclusion that restates your view.
checklist: I used at least three precise, interesting words
I varied how my sentences start
I checked spelling and punctuation at the end
I answered one argument from the other side
questions.technique: Opinion, reasons with examples, counter-argument, conclusion.
questions.source: ACER SEHS skill description: Writing, two tasks in 40 minutes
